definitions.definition: The puzzle of how a quantum system goes from being in many possible states at once to just one definite state when measured.
definitions.example: Like a spinning coin that is both heads and tails until you slap it down on your hand.

definitions.definition: A quantum state where a particle exists in all possible states at the same time until it is measured.
definitions.example: Like a musical chord that contains several notes played together, not just one note.

definitions.definition: The study of the basic principles and assumptions behind quantum mechanics.
definitions.example: Like asking what the rules of a board game really mean, not just how to play.

definitions.definition: An experiment where particles like electrons are shot at a barrier with two slits, showing they act like waves until observed.
definitions.example: Like throwing marbles at a fence with two holes and seeing a wave pattern on the other side, which is weird for marbles.

definitions.definition: Experiments where the decision to measure a particle is made after it has already passed through the slits, still affecting its behavior.
definitions.example: Like deciding to look at a coin after it has landed, but that decision somehow changes whether it was heads or tails.

definitions.definition: The idea that a quantum system is in all states until a measurement forces it into one, but it does not clearly define what a measurement is.
definitions.example: Like saying a pizza is both pepperoni and cheese until you take a bite, but not explaining what counts as a bite.

definitions.definition: The idea that every possible outcome of a quantum event actually happens, each in its own separate universe.
definitions.example: Like every time you flip a coin, two universes split off: one where it lands heads, one where it lands tails.

definitions.definition: The process where a quantum system loses its superposition and appears classical because it interacts with its environment.
definitions.example: Like ripples in a pond smoothing out when wind and debris disturb the water.

definitions.definition: Theories that say quantum systems collapse into one state on their own, due to some physical mechanism, not because of measurement.
definitions.example: Like saying a spinning coin automatically falls flat after a certain time, no matter if you catch it or not.

definitions.definition: A logical mistake where an argument assumes the very thing it is trying to prove.
definitions.example: Saying 'this drug works because it is effective' just restates the claim without evidence.

definitions.definition: An endless chain where each step depends on the next, never reaching a final answer.
definitions.example: Like saying 'I need a friend to help me make friends, but I need a friend to get that friend' — it never ends.

definitions.definition: The process of making a possibility into a real, definite event.
definitions.example: Like choosing one flavor of ice cream from a menu and actually scooping it into a cone.

definitions.definition: Three distinct roles or functions that work together as one single action.
definitions.example: Like a three-person relay race where each runner has a different job but together they complete one race.

definitions.definition: The Christian belief that God is one being in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
definitions.example: Like water that can be liquid, ice, and steam — three forms, one substance.

definitions.definition: A Greek word meaning 'word', 'reason', or 'order', used in Christian theology to describe Jesus as the divine pattern of creation.
definitions.example: Like the blueprint or logic that makes a building stand up straight.

definitions.definition: A mathematical space used in quantum mechanics to describe all possible states of a system.
definitions.example: Like a giant library where every possible book (state) has its own shelf.

definitions.definition: A smooth, reversible change of a quantum system described by the Schrödinger equation, preserving total probability.
definitions.example: Like a perfectly elastic ball bouncing without losing any energy.

definitions.definition: A set of special states (eigenstates) that form a reference frame for measuring a quantum property.
definitions.example: Like a set of standard rulers for measuring length in inches or centimeters.

definitions.definition: A definite state of a quantum system that yields a specific value when measured.
definitions.example: Like a coin that is definitely heads, not a mix of heads and tails.

definitions.definition: An infinite series of observers, each measuring the previous one, never reaching a final collapse.
definitions.example: Like a line of people each looking at the person in front, but no one actually sees the original event.

definitions.definition: A quantum connection where two particles share a state, so measuring one instantly affects the other, no matter how far apart.
definitions.example: Like a pair of magic dice that always show the same number, even if rolled in different rooms.

definitions.definition: A mathematical operation that picks out one specific state from a superposition, like collapsing a wavefunction.
definitions.example: Like shining a flashlight on one object in a dark room full of objects.

definitions.definition: A measure of the size or length of a vector, in quantum mechanics related to total probability (which must be 1).
definitions.example: Like the total length of an arrow; if it changes, the arrow is not just rotating.

definitions.definition: A process that can be undone, returning the system to its original state without any loss of information.
definitions.example: Like freezing water into ice and then melting it back to water.

definitions.definition: A process that cannot be undone, like breaking an egg or mixing two colors of paint.
definitions.example: Like scrambling an egg — you cannot unscramble it.

definitions.definition: A property of equations where the output is directly proportional to the input, without any squaring or other complications.
definitions.example: Like doubling the ingredients in a recipe doubles the amount of cake.

definitions.definition: A system where the future is completely determined by the present, with no randomness.
definitions.example: Like a clock: if you know the time now, you can predict exactly what it will be in one hour.

definitions.definition: A process that does not preserve total probability, often associated with irreversible collapse in quantum mechanics.
definitions.example: Like a leaky bucket that loses water — the total amount changes.

definitions.definition: A single operation made by combining two or more simpler operations in a specific order.
definitions.example: Like putting on socks then shoes — two steps that together make one action: getting dressed.

definitions.definition: Something that does not need anything outside itself to work or be complete.
definitions.example: Like a Swiss Army knife that has a blade, scissors, and a corkscrew all in one tool.

definitions.definition: Extra parts that are not strictly necessary but may provide backup or safety.
definitions.example: Like having two spare tires in your car when you only need one.

definitions.definition: A structure that cannot be simplified to fewer than three parts, yet those three parts function as one whole.
definitions.example: Like a three-legged stool: remove one leg and it falls, but all three together make one stable seat.
